title: The Unquiet Witness
premise: When the coffin of Ashford's revered founder, Edmund Voss, is exhumed for a bicentennial ceremony and found empty, coroner Hazel Iversen recognizes a pattern: three 'accidental' deaths in the past year all involved people connected to Voss's estate. As Hazel digs into the town's founding myth, they discover the founder never died here at all — his body was hidden decades ago by someone still alive and powerful. The killer, a descendant protecting the family's darkest secret, begins eliminating witnesses faster than Hazel can find them. In the end, Hazel stages their own death using their knowledge of every grave in town, luring the killer into confessing over an empty casket — and finds a new family among the outcasts who helped them survive.
about_author: I. M. Delacroix is the pen name of a former rural mortuary assistant who spent a decade listening to small towns talk around their dead. They write mysteries about the people history buries twice.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Hazel Iversen's POV. During preparations for Ashford's bicentennial, Hazel quietly closes their fourth unexplained case file, uneasy that police keep ruling deaths accidental. A chance remark from gravedigger Tomás Okafor about disturbed soil near the Voss mausoleum plants the first seed of doubt. Emotional beat: lonely competence — Hazel knows the town better than it knows itself, and it costs them.

chapters.title: The Empty Coffin
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The ceremonial exhumation of founder Edmund Voss reveals a coffin filled with weighted sandbags and a century-old lie. Councilwoman Marguerite Voss demands the matter buried quietly; Police Chief Dunmore obeys. Hazel refuses to sign the falsified report. Emotional beat: the thrill of confirmation curdling into isolation as the town's institutions close ranks.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: Alternating Hazel and archivist Priya Raman's POV. Priya, who catalogued the Voss papers, shows Hazel how the three prior 'accidents' each removed someone who'd handled estate documents. The pattern is deliberate, professional, and recent. Emotional beat: found-family spark — two outsiders realize they've been investigating alone what they should have faced together.

chapters.title: The Founder's Shadow
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Deep in the archives, Priya uncovers evidence Voss died elsewhere under another name, his return staged to sanctify the family dynasty. That night her office is ransacked and her research stolen — but she mailed a copy to Hazel first. Emotional beat: dread arriving on schedule; the killer is always one step ahead because he wrote the file.

chapters.title: What the Dead Keep
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel re-examines remains from the earlier cases and finds staging errors only a coroner would catch — the killer has medical training or access. Suspicion falls on town physician Dr. Alden Voss, Marguerite's brother, who offers Hazel a promotion and a warning in the same breath. Emotional beat: temptation and threat braided together; power makes its offer politely.

chapters.title: A Grave for the Living
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. Tomás reveals he saw someone burying a fresh package in potter's field weeks ago and kept silent out of fear. He and Hazel exhume it: Edmund Voss's actual remains, hidden by an ancestor to conceal how he truly died — poisoned by his own heirs. Emotional beat: grief for the long-dead man used as a prop, and Tomás choosing courage after a lifetime of looking away.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Confession
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Confronted, Marguerite admits the family secret but swears she isn't the killer — her brother Alden has been 'protecting' the legacy for years, and she's been paying for his silence. Before Hazel can act, Marguerite is found drowned in her bath, ruled natural. Emotional beat: the sickening cost of hesitation; survival has a price and someone else paid it.

chapters.title: The Trap Is Set
chapters.summary: Priya and Tomás's POV. Knowing Alden reads every official channel, the trio feeds him a false report: Hazel has located a living witness with documentary proof and will meet them at the mausoleum. Meanwhile Hazel prepares their own 'death' — a closed-casket burial they alone could fake. Emotional beat: taut camaraderie; the found family becomes a hunting pack.

chapters.title: Ashes and Testimony
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, climax. At the mausoleum, Alden arrives to kill the witness and instead finds Hazel alive beside an open coffin, recorder running. He confesses to four murders across two generations of cover-ups, then attacks; Tomás and Priya intervene, and Chief Dunmore — finally choosing the town over the family — makes the arrest. Emotional beat: fury transmuted into justice; the dead finally testify.

chapters.title: The Unquiet Witness
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, resolution. Weeks later, Edmund Voss is buried properly under his true name, and Hazel signs reports no one can bury. The town is shaken but honest for the first time in a century. Hazel, once solitary, shares a late dinner with Priya and Tomás in the records room. Emotional beat: quiet belonging — the price of survival was paid, and what it bought was family.
